brief.default.closing: anyone may post a message starting with "PLAN vN: " (with the colon); the others amend it with a vN+1 or vote "VOTE vN: yes, checked <file:line, output, #n>" / "VOTE vN: no, because <evidence>", each vote as the first line of its own message. A yes without what it rests on does not count; a no always stops the closing, and without evidence the LEAD asks for it. When one version has a yes from everyone, its author posts CLOSED vN (chat.py refuses it before) and everyone stops. A no is a split: the LEAD reviews it and decides. After PLAN v3 only the LEAD posts a new version.

cmd.accelera.label: Speed up and anticipate steps, same quality
cmd.accelera.name: speedup
cmd.accelera.text: @all SPEED UP. Time matters: do not spend time that can be avoided, and the earlier a correct result arrives, the better. Make routine decisions yourself and keep going; stop only when different readings would lead to really different work. While something runs, prepare the next step. When two actions do not depend on each other, do them together in the same turn. Quality does not drop: the planned checks stay, but do not re-check what is already verified. Do not spawn subagents: you do the work yourself.
cmd.aiutatevi.label: Who waits helps a teammate (the lead pairs)
cmd.aiutatevi.name: helpout
cmd.aiutatevi.text: @all HELP EACH OTHER (the lead pairs you). Whoever is idle or waiting posts a --status in JSON with "free_min" (the minutes you expect to wait still) and in "step" what you can do, then goes back to --idle. Whoever works says in one line what could be split off ("SPLITTABLE T3: what, ~N min, files ...") or "nothing to split". The lead pairs you with chat.py helpers: a long wait takes a lot, a short one a little (under 10 min a review, a proof to redo or a test; 10-30 min a piece of a task; over 30 min a whole task). For each pair the one who works writes the packet: task help T3 NAME --scope "what is in, what is out" --files a,b --done-when "the proof expected" --note "decisions, where to read (file:line), what was tried"; or says "no thanks" when explaining costs more than doing. The helper changes only those files and closes with task done Tn --proof; if its own wait ends first, task giveback Tn --note "where I got to". The lender does not touch the lent files until the packet is back. Shared files still go through the lead.
cmd.consegna.label: Converge on the delivery
cmd.consegna.name: deliver
cmd.consegna.text: @all TOWARD THE DELIVERY. No new ideas and no widening of scope: finish what is open. Whoever has the fullest picture writes the draft (done, evidence, numbers, open points); the others amend it or vote within a few messages. What does not fit goes to the open points or to the ideas for the lead.
cmd.menoparole.label: A little less talk, a little more work
cmd.menoparole.name: lesstalk
cmd.menoparole.text: @all A little less talk and a little more work (not drastically). Write when you have a result, a finding that changes something, a change of direction or a question that blocks you. Do not announce what you are about to do: do it. No repeating what was already said, no thanks or redundant summaries. Statuses stay, in one or two lines with the percentage. Always answer when someone tags you.
cmd.pausa.label: Finish the step, save the state, go idle
cmd.pausa.name: pause
cmd.pausa.text: @all PAUSE. Finish the step in progress without leaving files half done. Then each of you writes where you got to (percentage, what is missing, how to resume) and goes idle with --idle until tagged.
cmd.prove.label: Back every claim with evidence
cmd.prove.name: evidence
cmd.prove.text: @all EVIDENCE. Every recent claim that still has no evidence gets it now: a picture with --image, a measurement with numbers and load, or file:line, in a JSON status ({"task": "T…", "pct": N, "evidence": ["…"]}); a task you closed gets its --proof (task done T… --proof). What cannot be proven is written as "not verified", without rounding up.
cmd.resoconto.label: A short report from everyone
cmd.resoconto.name: report
cmd.resoconto.text: @all REPORT for the user. Each of you posts ONE JSON status (post --status, the text starts with {): {"task": "T…", "pct": N, "done": "the outcome: what you did, what you found", "evidence": ["file:line, #message, picture, measure"], "risks": "what is missing or fragile", "needs": "what you need from whom", "next": "your next action"}. Numbers and evidence instead of adjectives. Then go straight back to work.
cmd.soccorso.label: Who waits helps the other room (the lead pairs)
cmd.soccorso.name: helpacross
cmd.soccorso.text: @all HELP THE OTHER ROOM (the lead pairs you). Whoever is idle or waiting here posts a --status in JSON with "free_min" and in "step" what you can do, then goes back to --idle. The lead looks at the other room too and pairs you with one of its people: the packet is written there, on that room's board (task help with your name), and the lead tells you the room folder. You read it with board --room <that room>, change only the files of the packet, and in that room's chat write only about the packet (post --room <that room> --as you, tagging who gave it to you); close with task done Tn --proof "the proof" --room <that room>, or task giveback Tn --room <that room> as soon as your own wait ends, and come back here. No shared files, no other work over there.
